summary: Fred Pfeil worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned his undergraduate degree at Amherst College (~1967–1971) and an M.A. at Stanford (~1971–1973). He taught at Stanford, Stephens College, Oregon State University, and Trinity College (~1983–2005).

Freda Bedi worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at St Hugh's College (~1929–1933) and under Mahasi Sayadaw (~1952–1954). She founded the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling.

Linguist Frederick James Furnivall studied at University College London and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served as Secretary of the Philological Society (1853–1910) and editor of the Oxford English Dictionary (1861–1870), and founded several literary and text societies.
Frederick M. Asher was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He held an academic post at the University of Minnesota from around 1972 to 2017, serving as Professor from roughly 1985 to 2017.
Frederick M. Smith works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Ludo Rocher and served as a professor at the University of Iowa (attested 2006–2008).

Frederick William Thomas specialized in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell, served at the India Office Library (1898–1927), and was Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1927 to 1937.

Frederik David Kan Bosch was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He led the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (~1916–1936) and later held posts at Utrecht University (1938–1945) and Leiden University (1946–1957).

Fredrik Barth studied at the University of Chicago and under Edmund Leach at Cambridge. He held professorships at the University of Bergen (1961–1972), University of Oslo (1974), and Boston University (~1997–2008), and taught at Emory and Harvard.

Friederike Assandri specializes in Sinology and religious studies. She completed PhD studies under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer at the University of Heidelberg, where she also held a post attested in 2013.

Friedhelm Hardy worked in Indology and religious studies. He completed doctoral work at the University of Oxford in 1967, served as Professor of Indian Religions at King's College London (~1975–2004), and was Wilde Lecturer at Oxford (1985–1987).

Scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies Friedrich Alexander Bischoff studied at Paris under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He held professorships at Indiana University (1964–1982), University of Hamburg (1982–1993), and University of Vienna (~1983–2009).

Indologist and linguist Friedrich August Rosen studied at Leipzig and in Berlin under Franz Bopp. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at University College London (1828–1831) and held the Sanskrit professorship at the University of London from 1834.

Friedrich August Wolf worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen (~1777–1779) and held a post at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from roughly 1783 to 1807.

Friedrich Bechtel worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and August Fick, taught at Göttingen (1884), and served as professor of comparative linguistics at the University of Halle from 1895.

Friedrich Benedict Weber studied at the University of Leipzig (~1792–1796). He held a post at the University of Frankfurt (Oder) (~1802–1811) and served as professor of political economy at the University of Breslau from roughly 1811 to 1848.

Friedrich Bollensen worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald, taught at Gatchina, was an adjunct professor at Saint Petersburg (~1844–1860), and served as professor of Sanskrit at Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).
Friedrich Brockhaus held professorships at the University of Jena (~1868–1871), the University of Basel (~1871–1872), Kiel University (~1872–1888), and the University of Marburg (~1888–1889).

Friedrich Carl Andreas worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1868–1870), he held posts at the University of Berlin (~1897–1903) and the University of Göttingen (~1903–1930).

Linguist Friedrich Christian Diez studied at the University of Giessen (~1811–1813) and the University of Göttingen (~1813–1818). He held a long-term academic post at the University of Bonn from approximately 1823 to 1876.

Friedrich Creuzer was a scholar of religious studies, history/archaeology, and philosophy. He studied at Jena and Tübingen, then held posts at the University of Marburg (~1802–1804), Leiden University (1809), and the University of Heidelberg (~1804–1845).
